A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HELM study. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding equations, tables and figures can be matched despite additions, relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Hamiltonian-prediction benchmarks, energy-pretraining experiments and embedding analyses in Sections 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds component ablations in Appendix C.3 and electron-density comparisons in Figure 13.

M1.justification: HELM's backbone, output heads, losses and pretraining procedures are retained. Node-parity expansion and scalar normalization were already described in v1 Sections 3 and B.3; v2 tests these existing components rather than introducing them.

E1.justification: The MD17/QM7, ∇2DFT and OMol dataset coverage is retained. Figure 13 adds qualitative evaluation of reconstructed electron densities, modestly extending the evaluated properties beyond the previously reported Hamiltonian matrices, eigenvalues and energies.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains SchNOrb, PhiSNet, QHNet and SPHNet with unchanged dataset participation. The direct, pretrained-frozen and finetuned comparisons also remain unchanged; the new component-removal controls are internal ablations.

E3.justification: Appendix C.3 introduces a separate four-configuration ablation protocol on ∇2DFT's 2k splits, using 500 epochs and a cosine scheduler. It explicitly distinguishes this unconverged protocol from the retained Table 2 training settings. Figure 13 additionally evaluates one illustrated molecule from each dataset.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.3 supplies a controlled factorial ablation of node-parity expansion and scalar normalization, substantially strengthening component-level analysis absent from v1. Appendix D.2 also adds three qualitative electron-density case studies comparing predicted and reference Hamiltonians.

E5.justification: Tables 3 and 4 retain the same 95% confidence-interval reporting. No repeated-run counts, seed information, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures are added or revised; the new ablation table reports point estimates.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and pretraining values are unchanged, including v1 Table 9, now v2 Table 10. New Table 9 reports fixed-budget ablation results: test Hamiltonian/energy errors are 324.35 μEh/329,923.53 meV with both components disabled and 96.27 μEh/706.39 meV with both enabled. Figure 13 adds qualitative density-agreement findings.

T1.justification: The architectural equations, parity constraint, DFT derivations, orbital decomposition and normalization formulas are retained. The new ablation explanations introduce no formal definitions, assumptions, proofs or mathematical corrections.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion are unchanged, retaining the claims about Hamiltonian prediction, chemical coverage and low-data energy pretraining. The introduction's added sentence identifies existing scalability mechanisms without redefining the contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 newly explains how large diagonal Hamiltonian entries and scalar dynamic range affect reconstructed energy accuracy, attributing improvements to parity handling and normalization. It also explicitly qualifies the ablations as generally unconverged after 500 epochs.

D1.justification: Table 2's caption clarifies that energy reconstruction uses each dataset's functional. The density analysis specifies PySCF and lists visualization isovalues in Figure 13. Existing implementation tables and code/data availability statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list and related-work discussion are unchanged. The additional introductory citation to Passaro and Zitnick references work already cited and discussed in v1.

P1.justification: v2 adds Appendix C.3, brief explanatory sentences and cross-references, and a short density-analysis paragraph. A UMAP interpretation sentence is simplified, while the overall organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the ablation Table 9 and electron-density Figure 13, adjusts existing figure rendering and sizing, and relocates some appendix displays. The earlier cross-split table and UMAP figures are retained with new numbering; there is no broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful empirical support for two previously unablated design choices through Appendix C.3 and adds qualitative evidence of reconstructed density fidelity. These strengthen the paper without changing its main results. The gains remain limited because the ablations use one split with explicitly unconverged training, and the density assessment consists of three visual examples.
